lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say what you have, need and want at the table and ask if there is a table or a wait.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Ask the host if there is a table for your group, say you have a reservation, and ask if you have to wait.
lessons.title: A Table, a Reservation, and What You Need
lessons.objective: Ask whether a table is available, say what you have and need, and request a dish or drink in French.
lessons.focus: Use il y a for “there is,” nous avons for “we have,” and nous avons besoin de for “we need.” Je voudrais is a polite request, while faut-il attendre ? asks whether waiting is necessary. After besoin de, say d'une chaise or de pain as the noun requires.
lessons.scene: Sam's party arrives early; Camille checks the terrace and brings another chair.

cards.fr: Est-ce qu'il y a une table pour deux ?
cards.en: Is there a table for two?

cards.fr: Nous avons une réservation au nom de Smith.
cards.en: We have a reservation under Smith's name.

cards.fr: Nous avons besoin d'une chaise, s'il vous plaît.
Je voudrais le vin rouge de la maison.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonsoir. Est-ce qu'il y a une table pour deux ?
reader.en: Good evening. Is there a table for two?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Oui, il y a une table en terrasse.
reader.en: Yes, there is a table on the terrace.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Nous avons une réservation au nom de Smith. Faut-il attendre longtemps ?
reader.en: We have a reservation under Smith's name. Do we have to wait long?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Non, la table est prête. Il vous faut autre chose ?
reader.en: No, the table is ready. Do you need anything else?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Nous avons besoin d'une chaise, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: We need a chair, please.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bien sûr. Voici la chaise et la carte des vins.
reader.en: Of course. Here is the chair and the wine list.

reader.speaker: Sam

reader.en: I would like the house red wine. We would like a starter to share.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Très bien. Je vous apporte aussi du pain.
reader.en: Very well. I'll also bring you some bread.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say where you are going, what you plan to do and ask what you can do at dinner.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the host you are going to wait at the bar and that you are going to celebrate something, then ask if you can make a toast.
lessons.title: Where We Are Going and What We Can Do
lessons.objective: Say where you will wait, what you plan to celebrate, and ask what is possible at dinner.
lessons.focus: Use aller + infinitive for a near-future plan: je vais attendre, nous allons fêter. Pouvoir asks what is possible: est-ce qu'on peut porter un toast ? Faire names an action, while sans ail states a precise ingredient omission.
lessons.scene: Sam and Léa wait at the bar before an anniversary dinner.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say what you and others eat, drink and share using present-tense verbs.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell a dining companion what you eat and drink, ask what they eat, and say what you are sharing.
lessons.title: What We Eat, Drink, and Share
lessons.objective: Say what you eat and drink, ask a companion what they eat, and describe a shared dish in the French present tense.
lessons.focus: With manger, je mange and tu manges have different spellings but the same spoken ending; nous mangeons keeps the soft g. Partager gives nous partageons. Boire is irregular: je bois, tu bois. Use vous mangez with someone you address formally.
lessons.scene: Sam and Léa compare dinner choices and order a shared salad.

cards.fr: Je bois de l'eau gazeuse, merci.
cards.en: I'll have sparkling water, thank you.

cards.fr: Tu manges des fruits de mer ?
Qu'est-ce qu'il y a dans la soupe ?

cards.en: People eat dinner very late here.

reader.en: Are you eating seafood tonight?

reader.en: No, I'm eating fish and vegetables.

reader.speaker: Léa
reader.fr: Moi, je bois de l'eau gazeuse. Et toi ?
reader.en: I'm having sparkling water. And you?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Je bois aussi de l'eau. Nous partageons la salade ?
reader.en: I'm also having water. Shall we share the salad?

reader.speaker: Léa
reader.fr: Oui. Qu'est-ce qu'il y a dans la soupe ?
reader.en: Yes. What's in the soup?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Il y a des légumes et du fromage.
reader.en: There are vegetables and cheese.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Vous faites griller le poisson ?
reader.en: Do you grill the fish?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Oui. Ici, on dîne très tard, mais la cuisine est déjà ouverte.
reader.en: Yes. People eat dinner very late here, but the kitchen is already open.

internalReviewNotes: Qualified French review is required for naturalness, local restaurant register, and variant answers before release.

Foundation 5 renders the source's culture-specific sobremesa as an explanatory French phrase rather than borrowing a Spanish term. The dinner speaking task preserves the bar/celebration/toast outcome.
Foundation 6 teaches the French present tense through manger, partager, and irregular boire rather than reproducing Spanish conjugation classes.
